recorded: Every case passed against the original with Node.js 26.12.1, fastify 5.7.4, @fastify/multipart 9.4.0, @langchain/core 1.1.27, @langchain/langgraph 1.1.5, @langchain/openai 1.2.9, langchain 1.2.25, and zod 3.25.76, installed from the module's lockfile and run as "node src/index.ts" without a .env file, so LangSmith tracing stays off. The original always listens on port 4000 and always calls OpenRouter's address, so the copy that produced these cases listens on PORT, falling back to 4000, a one-line change in src/index.ts that leaves the banner naming 4000, and passes OPENAI_BASE_URL to ChatOpenAI as its base URL, falling back to OpenRouter's, a one-line change in src/services/openrouterService.ts. At startup the server sends its own route the PDF in docs/ through Fastify's inject and prints the answer, so every case waits for that answer and expects that request first, and a transcription keeps the docs folder beside its source. That request carries the whole 443686-byte PDF in base64, which the cases check by its first and last 64 characters and its length. The uploads are a one-page PDF of meeting notes written for these cases. No OpenRouter key was available, and Ollama rejects a PDF in an image_url part as an invalid image, so no stand-in model can answer the request the program sends. Every answer is therefore synthesized in OpenRouter's documented response format, with a text written from the PDF's text, extracted with PDFKit (the title, authors, abstract, introduction, and figures of the first two pages for the course's document), while the requests keep the model, the routing, and the parts the program sends. The rejected key comes from OpenRouter's documented error format, and the message it leaves in the answer, the runtime's own, is checked by the status code on its first line. Every upload puts the question before the file or after a small one, because @fastify/multipart never sees a question that follows a file larger than its stream buffer, which is not what the handler means. No case sends a file over the 10 MB limit, which ends in the same 500 as a body that is not multipart, or depends on the letter case or parameters of a media type. The LangGraph CLI's development server, which factory.ts and langgraph.json register the graph for, belongs to the CLI and has no cases.

This document is **"A Comprehensive Overview of Large Language Models"**, a survey paper by Humza Naveed, Asad Ullah Khan, Shi Qiu, Muhammad Saqib, Saeed Anwar, Muhammad Usman, Naveed Akhtar, Nick Barnes, and Ajmal Mian, from universities and research centers in Australia, Pakistan, Hong Kong, and Saudi Arabia (arXiv:2307.06435v10, October 2024).

Here's what it contains:

*   **Abstract:** LLM research is moving so fast that it is hard to see the bigger picture, so the paper offers a concise yet comprehensive overview that works both as a systematic survey and as a quick reference for researchers and practitioners.
*   **Introduction:** how natural language processing evolved from statistical and neural language models to pre-trained language models and then to LLMs, and why fine-tuning with instructions and alignment with human preferences improve them.
*   **Figures:** a chart of the papers released each year from 2018 to 2024 about LLMs, fine-tuning, and alignment, and a timeline of LLM releases, from T5 and GPT-3 to LLaMA 3, Gemini-1.5, and OpenAI o1, split into pre-trained and instruction-tuned, open-source and closed-source models.
*   **Topics covered:** architectural innovations, training strategies, context length improvements, fine-tuning, multimodal and augmented LLMs, robotics, datasets, benchmarking, efficiency, applications, and challenges.

Keywords include Large Language Models, chatGPT, Augmented LLMs, Multimodal LLMs, LLM training, and LLM Benchmarking.
